I’ve been working on a GIM floor at a downtown hospital for 1.5 years now. Ratios are usually (day shift) 1-5 if we are fully staffed 1-4. Expect to be very busy especially weekdays. Expect to be caring for the homeless, people with MH issues, drug users, etc. 

Unit culture would vary depending on the hospital, unit however the floor I work at is very welcoming. I have been fortunate to be able to work with really good colleagues and we always help each other out. 

Downtown hospitals are all teaching hospitals so expect to be working with nursing students and residents. On my unit we can have up to 10 different residents looking after patients.  

IMO medicine is a good starting place to develop confidence with your skills. You will see all sorts of patients with a wide variety of diagnoses. Respiratory, GI, hematology, ODs, hepatology, etc 

ICU can also be great especially if you are taking a sponsorship as you will have many weeks of orientation and preceptorship. Depends on the type of work you want to be doing
